construct: ROMK recycles potassium from thick ascending limb cells back into the tubular lumen, sustaining luminal potassium needed for NKCC2 activity and the lumen-positive transepithelial voltage. KCNJ1 loss therefore reduces NaCl reabsorption, increases distal sodium delivery, activates renin-aldosterone signaling, and causes salt wasting, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, and hypercalciuria.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Antenatal salt wasting with polyhydramnios, hypokalemic alkalosis, high renin/aldosterone, hypercalciuria, normal blood pressure, and biallelic KCNJ1 variants identifies ROMK-dependent Bartter type 2.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: NKCC2 loss causes a very similar antenatal Bartter phenotype, but the KCNJ1 genotype specifically identifies the apical ROMK potassium-recycling defect.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The named KCNJ1 loss-of-function variant makes ROMK recycling the unique direct transport defect.
